items.sentence: Last night Jom ___ to the barangay court to play basketball.
items.why: 'Went' is the simple past; 'gone' needs a helper like 'has' or 'had'.

items.sentence: Lyka has ___ all the pancit before her brother got home.
items.why: After 'has', use the past participle 'eaten', not 'ate'.

items.sentence: The typhoon ___ around midnight, so classes were cancelled.
items.why: With no helper verb, use the simple past 'began'; 'begun' needs 'has' or 'had'.

items.sentence: Tita Nena ___ pasalubong from Dubai for the whole family.
items.why: 'Bring' is irregular, so its past form is 'brought'.

items.sentence: Marco ___ the ball just before it hit the tricycle.
items.why: The past of 'catch' is the irregular form 'caught'.

items.sentence: Kuya Ron ___ the empty load card into the trash.
items.why: The simple past of 'throw' is 'threw'; 'thrown' needs a helper verb.

items.sentence: Bea had already ___ to the sari-sari store when the rain started.
items.why: After 'had', use the past participle 'gone', not 'went'.

items.sentence: The movie had ___ before Jom found his seat in the cinema.
items.why: After 'had', use the past participle 'begun'; 'began' never follows a helper.

items.sentence: Jom and ___ waited for the jeepney for almost an hour.
items.why: In a compound subject use 'I', because you would say 'I waited'.

items.sentence: Tita Nena sent the balikbayan box to Lyka and ___.
items.why: After 'to', use the object pronoun 'me'; test it by dropping 'Lyka and'.

items.sentence: The coach gave the extra jerseys to ___ after practice.
items.why: After a preposition like 'to', use the object form 'us'.

items.sentence: Marco hurt ___ when he slid on the wet court.
items.why: When the subject and object are the same person, use the reflexive 'himself'.

items.sentence: Bea finished the whole project by ___ while the others were offline.
items.why: 'By herself' means alone, so use the reflexive 'herself'.

items.sentence: The players blamed ___ for losing the barangay finals.
items.why: When the subject and object are the same people, use 'themselves'.

items.sentence: Kuya Ron and ___ fixed the tricycle engine before the fiesta.
items.why: In a compound subject use 'he', because you would say 'he fixed'.

items.sentence: Everyone except Lyka and ___ passed the science quiz.
items.why: 'Except' is a preposition, so it takes the object pronoun 'me'.

items.sentence: Lyka sings so ___ that the whole barangay asked her to perform.
items.why: 'Well' is the adverb that tells how she sings; 'good' describes a noun.

items.sentence: Marco felt ___ about missing his mother's video call from Dubai.
items.why: After a linking verb like 'felt', use the adjective 'bad'.

items.sentence: The jeepney driver turned ___ to avoid the deep pothole.
items.why: 'Quickly' is an adverb because it tells how he turned.

items.sentence: The adobo at Tita Nena's carinderia always tastes ___.
items.why: 'Tastes' is a linking verb, so it takes the adjective 'good'.

items.sentence: Jom played ___ in the second half, so the coach benched him.
items.why: 'Badly' is the adverb that tells how he played.

items.sentence: The signal in our barangay is ___ slow during typhoons.
items.why: Use the adverb 'really' to describe the adjective 'slow'.

items.sentence: The new teacher seems ___, but her quizzes are difficult.
items.why: 'Seems' is a linking verb, so it takes the adjective 'nice'.

items.sentence: The jeepney smelled ___ after the fish delivery this morning.
items.why: 'Smelled' is a linking verb here, so use the adjective 'bad'.

items.sentence: Jeepney fare is ___ than tricycle fare in our barangay.
items.why: With 'than', use the comparative 'cheaper'; short words take '-er', not 'more'.

items.sentence: Marco is the ___ player on the whole barangay team.
items.why: Comparing three or more, use the superlative 'tallest'.

items.sentence: Lyka's phone is ___ than mine, but hers has no load.
items.why: Long adjectives use 'more' when comparing two things.

items.sentence: Jom's cough got ___ after he played in the rain.
items.why: The comparative of 'bad' is 'worse'.

items.sentence: This is the ___ adobo I have ever tasted at any fiesta.
items.why: The superlative of 'good' is 'best'.

items.sentence: Online games are ___ interesting than our science module, honestly.
items.why: 'More ... than' compares two things.

items.sentence: Bea's three-point shot is ___ than Marco's.
items.why: 'Better' is already comparative, so never say 'more better'.

items.sentence: Of all the typhoons this year, Enteng was the ___.
items.why: 'Of all' signals the superlative, so use 'strongest' with no extra 'most'.

items.sentence: Jom wanted to play, ___ his mother told him to finish his homework first.
items.why: 'But' joins two ideas that go against each other.

items.sentence: We stayed inside ___ the typhoon signal was raised to number three.
items.why: 'Because' gives the reason for staying inside.

items.sentence: You cannot join the online match ___ you buy load first.
items.why: 'Unless' means 'if not': no load, no match.

items.sentence: ___ Lyka was tired, she still helped Tita Nena at the store.
items.why: 'Although' shows a surprise: she was tired, but she still helped.

items.sentence: Marco lost his jeepney fare, ___ he walked all the way to school.
items.why: 'So' shows the result of losing the fare.

items.sentence: Bea scrolled TikTok ___ her classmates copied the assignment.
items.why: 'While' means at the same time.

items.sentence: Will you ride the tricycle ___ walk to the barangay hall?
items.why: 'Or' offers a choice between two actions.

items.sentence: Kuya Ron bought pandesal ___ a bottle of Coke for our merienda.
items.why: 'And' simply adds one item to another.
